design.question: Does the headline CURVE_ESTABLISHED margin at 4096 (0003: +0.1003 over the frozen baseline set, +0.0583 over all baselines) survive the budgeted, symmetric recipe search that moved the 2048 margin from +0.0475 (0011) to +0.0234 (0012, read under 0013)?
design.what_is_reused_from_0012: the runner, the roster (candidate for candidate; two 'why' strings corrected, see review), the chunk-rule holdout, the two stages, the tie rule, the two-invocation protocol, the floors mechanism, the reader structure (0013's, with the second-stage order line as fixed there)

pre_freeze_review.how: three independent refuters, each instructed to break the unfrozen package against the code, the cache and the container, followed by one synthesis; run on 2026-09-04 before the freeze

findings_adopted.finding: InPlaceScaled called numpy std(axis=0), which materialises a full-size float64 temporary: a second 7.09 GB copy of the 800000-row pool during the confirmatory standardised-logistic fit, against a 16.46 GB container with no swap and an observed kill ceiling near 13.9 GB anonymous. 0012 had banked the same temporary as +4.3 GB of ru_maxrss at 500000 rows without anyone reading it as such.
findings_adopted.fix: two-pass chunkwise mean and standard deviation over 20000-row passes (matches numpy to 1e-14 relative); a tracemalloc probe of the standardiser runs once per process and is banked in every record's environment

findings_adopted.finding: the heartbeat and the infeasible_memory stamp read VmRSS, which counts the file-backed pages of the 5.77 GB memory-mapped cache; a 14.5 GB threshold would be crossed by an idle confirm-stage process and could never witness a real kill at the 13.9 GB anonymous ceiling
findings_adopted.fix: heartbeat and stamp read anonymous RSS (RssAnon; VmRSS banked beside it); protocol.caps.memory_kill_gb 13.0 anonymous; launch.min_mem_available_gb 12.0; the cost paragraph restated in anonymous-memory terms with the heartbeat's 30 s blind spot stated

findings_adopted.finding: sealed fields carried 2048-era constants copied from 0012: the three 'must equal' split hashes, 113412 non-gutenberg rows, 5000 evaluation chunks, a 500000-row pool, a 12.5 GB threshold, 0012's boundary strings, the 0.0025 sentence, and '0003's CARVE_FAILS'
findings_adopted.fix: every constant replaced with the 4096 value the reader requires; a pre-freeze consistency script (scratchpad, not banked) asserts every sha256 and count quoted in the sealed text is a constant the reader carries, the protocol matches key by key, the roster hash matches, and no 2048-era token remains

findings_adopted.finding: two roster 'why' strings quoted 0011's banked baselines as 0003's (D1 '0.0887 banked', U2 '0.0385 banked')
findings_adopted.fix: 0.0969 and 0.0387; roster sha256 recomputed and the reader's ROSTER_SHA256 updated in the same commit

findings_adopted.finding: the runner's CLI defaults are 0012's banked paths and --smoke disabled the selection-exists refusal, so a smoke launched with the defaults would have overwritten a chain-referenced artifact; the smoke block had no invocation; smoke confirm stages score the sealed set and the disclosure did not count them
findings_adopted.fix: the runner refuses --smoke with any output under artifacts/ and a real run with any output outside it; smoke invocation added; the sealed-set disclosure counts smoke confirms and points here for their number

findings_adopted.finding: runner schema strings and the cluster-CI note named 2048 (5000 chunks); the reader's provenance comment said cap 500000 and 0012
findings_adopted.fix: derived from the run (output basename, partition n_eval_chunks); comment corrected

findings_adopted.finding: the cost block's worst case scaled all of 0012's worst case by 1.6 although stage 1 runs on the same rows; the cap is enforced before each fit so it can be exceeded by one fit; iteration counts at 4096 are unanchored; the HGB bin-mapper draws a 1.77 GB transient
findings_adopted.fix: stated as limits of the arithmetic in scope.cost, with the deep-tree headroom under the ceiling made explicit

findings_adopted.finding: Store.save writes a checkpoint and only then appends the 'completed' ledger event; a restart inside that window would leave a banked record with no completion event, which the reader counts as zero completions (never observed: 0012 banked 52 started / 50 completed / 2 counted interruptions)
findings_adopted.fix: on resume, a checkpoint with no completion event gets one reconstructed from the checkpoint's banked seconds, marked reconstructed_on_resume

findings_adopted.finding: the standardiser probe's einsum materialised the squared block, doubling the per-pass transient it banked
findings_adopted.fix: squares in place, one transient per pass; the banked production transient (0.177 GB per 20000-row pass) is now the measured one

operator_procedure.repeated_launches_of_one_fit: once any confirm checkpoint exists the three-launch NOT RUN rule is off by design; a fit that is killed within 30 s of its last heartbeat is never stamped infeasible_memory. Repeated launches of the same fit with no new checkpoint are therefore the operator's signal to stop and file the VOID that stop rules 3 and 10 prescribe, by hand, with the launches ledger as the evidence. With the corrected memory arithmetic no honest fit approaches the ceiling, so this is a stated procedure, not an expected path.
